name: Zuar
overview: Zuar was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, known primarily as the father of Nethanel. His mention is brief and specific, focusing on his paternal role within the genealogical records of Israel. There are no additional notes or details about his life or character beyond this relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Zuar means 'little one' in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to be given directly by God but reflects a common Semitic naming convention. The meaning provides a simple linguistic insight without further theological implications.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zuar as the father of Nethanel and as a descendant of the tribe of Issachar. No other family relationships are mentioned beyond these, maintaining a focused genealogical identity in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zuar's significance lies in his role as a patriarch within the tribe of Issachar, specifically as the father of Nethanel, who is enumerated in the census of Israel. This highlights the importance of familial lineage and tribal identity in the organization and history of God's people. Though briefly mentioned, Zuar contributes to the continuity of God's covenant people through his offspring.
